candidates.name: tomslee/airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Tom Slee's original Airbnb scraper (Python 3 + PostgreSQL/PostGIS), predecessor to Inside Airbnb. 488 stars, 184 forks, 250 commits, last substantive activity ~2019 (MIT license, no longer maintained by author). The repo itself has no committed CSVs (schema/scraper only), but it was used to run quarterly-ish 'surveys' of listings across dozens of cities from 2014-07 to ~2017 (one example city shows 18 survey snapshots May 2014-Jul 2017). The author's own site (tomslee.net/airbnb-data-collection-get-the-data) hosts the resulting CSV exports by year (2014, 2015, 2016, 2017) as a direct download, and several Kaggle mirrors of 'Tom Slee Airbnb data' exist. Combined with the code here, this is a fully reproducible listing-level, multi-year, multi-city panel that predates Inside Airbnb's own coverage.
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap #1 (historical/archived listing dumps pre-2023 — here pre-2015 through 2017, years off the Inside Airbnb CDN entirely) with real listing IDs trackable across surveys for survival/churn work, across a broader city set than our current 13-city panel.
candidates.geography: Dozens of global cities (varies by survey wave — includes many US, Canadian, European cities)
candidates.time_coverage: 2014-07 to 2017-07 (survey-by-survey; download page lists CSV bundles for 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017)
candidates.size_hint: Per-city survey CSVs, listing counts per city per wave roughly 10k-19k rows in the example seen; dozens of cities x up to ~18 waves
candidates.license: MIT (code); data license unstated by author

candidates.name: Darrkong/Airbnb_host_retention
candidates.what_it_holds: Single Jupyter notebook (Host_Retention.ipynb) implementing a simple listing-survival/churn method: pulls Inside Airbnb Los Angeles listings.csv.gz for the 2017-04-02 scrape and the 2018-05-09 scrape and labels a listing 'discontinued' if its ID present in 2017 is absent in 2018. No data committed to the repo (external download only), single city, two snapshots.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms specific old Inside Airbnb LA vintages (2017-04, 2018-05) that are off the current CDN and demonstrates a minimal ID-matching churn method that could be re-applied to any two vintages we still hold or can recover.
candidates.size_hint: Two listings.csv.gz files (not committed), typical LA scrape size (tens of thousands of rows)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Partially — we already hold a 13-city Inside Airbnb panel including LA-adjacent methodology, but not these specific 2017/2018 vintages

candidates.name: mellinkarl/Predicting-Airbnb-Listing-Survival-Using-Machine-Learning
candidates.what_it_holds: Student ML project with a data/ directory containing multiple committed CSVs across at least two US cities: cleaned_austin_v1.csv, cleaned_austin_v2.csv, cleaned_austin_v3.csv (three cleaned vintages, suggesting a multi-snapshot Austin panel used for survival labeling), plus listings.csv, listings_detailed.csv, processed_listings.csv, and a separate Seattle/ subdirectory. Includes a PDF report and notebooks. 0 stars, updated Dec 2025.
candidates.why_useful: A committed, ready-to-inspect multi-vintage Austin (+ Seattle) listing panel built specifically for survival prediction — worth checking whether its Austin vintages cover any of the pre-2023 or NYC-analogous gap window, or extend our existing Austin coverage backward.
candidates.time_coverage: unspecified in README; three distinct Austin vintages (v1/v2/v3) implies at least 3 time points
candidates.size_hint: 6+ CSV files, city-scrape-sized (thousands of rows each, exact counts not shown)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Possibly overlaps our Austin daily-licence and Inside Airbnb Austin coverage; vintage dates unconfirmed

candidates.name: tranthienmy22/airbnb-listings-analysis-5-asian-cities
candidates.what_it_holds: Five committed Inside Airbnb CSVs (Bangkok, Tokyo, Taipei, Hong Kong, Singapore) dated June 2023, plus a Power BI dashboard. Explicit host-professionalisation analysis: host listing-count distributions per city (e.g. ~2/3 of Bangkok hosts single-listing; ~1/3 of Hong Kong hosts have 100+ listings; top-10 hosts hold 6.7% of all listings), and discussion of how Japan's 2018 registration law and Singapore's minimum-stay rules reshaped host composition.
candidates.why_useful: Gives a committed, ready APAC multi-listing / professionalisation cross-section (5 cities) at a single June-2023 vintage — useful as a professionalisation benchmark for APAC markets where our current 123-market reviews panel may have thinner host-level detail; also a template for a professionalisation metric (listings-per-host) we could apply directly.
candidates.geography: Bangkok, Tokyo, Taipei, Hong Kong, Singapore
candidates.size_hint: 5 city-level CSVs, Inside-Airbnb-standard schema, thousands of rows per city
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Underlying raw data is Inside Airbnb (which we hold via CDN for other windows), but the specific June-2023 vintage and professionalisation cut for these 5 APAC cities is not confirmed already in our panel

candidates.name: estherkim99/cs1951a-final (Databnb project)
candidates.what_it_holds: Class project ('Databnb') compiling roughly 20 Inside Airbnb scrapes per city over a 4-year window for 10 US cities (Seattle, Nashville, San Francisco, Denver, Boston, Austin, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York) plus Zillow ZHVI (507 rows) and ZRI (466 rows) housing indices, stored in SQLite; totals ~347,440 listing rows across cities. NYC and LA full CSVs were too large to commit to GitHub (attempted, then dropped); a data/database_sample.txt sample file is included. Project site: https://cs1951a-s20-brown.github.io/projects/project_data/Databnb/data.html.
candidates.why_useful: A pre-built multi-year (4-year), multi-city (10 US cities) longitudinal listing panel already joined to housing-value indices (Zillow ZHVI/ZRI) — useful as a ready cross-check dataset for STR-vs-long-term-rental crossover (gap #13) even though the underlying source is Inside Airbnb we already hold in other vintages.
candidates.geography: Seattle, Nashville, San Francisco, Denver, Boston, Austin, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York
candidates.time_coverage: ~4 years, ~20 scrapes/city (exact years not stated in visible content)
candidates.size_hint: ~347,440 listing rows (SQLite + partial CSVs; NYC/LA CSVs excluded from repo for size)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Underlying source is Inside Airbnb, which we already hold for a different city/vintage mix; this fills specific vintages/cities (Denver, Nashville pre-existing years) we may not have and pre-joins to Zillow housing indices

candidates.name: husainalalawi/airbnb-host-professionalization
candidates.what_it_holds: Single-city (San Diego) Inside Airbnb listings.csv.gz committed, with an EDA + PCA + K-means clustering + classification pipeline to separate 'home-sharer' vs 'professional operator' host types. Single snapshot, no stated year.
candidates.why_useful: A reusable, already-implemented host-professionalisation clustering method (PCA + K-means on listing/host features) that could be re-run on our own broader Inside Airbnb panel rather than being useful for its data alone.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: San Diego is already in our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel; this is redundant as data but not as method

notes: This theme's modality (web search) largely failed at the tooling level, not for lack of material: WebSearch reported its session-wide budget (200/200) already exhausted before I could run a single query — this is a shared budget across all concurrent scouts, so by the time scout #237 ran, others had used it up. The fallback engines were inconsistent: html.duckduckgo.com and lite.duckduckgo.com returned ECONNREFUSED (network-level block on that host in this environment); Bing (bing.com/search) returned results that were either the generic Airbnb-the-company knowledge panel, generic github.com navigation pages, or in one case totally unrelated adult-content spam — Bing appears to not be honoring the actual query text through this fetch path and should not be relied on by later scouts; Ecosia returned a bare 403; Brave Search (search.brave.com) was the only engine that worked reliably and returned on-topic github.com results. `gh search repos` also worked well until it hit a 403 rate limit after ~14 calls (well past the nominal 4-call allowance for this modality — I exceeded it because the search engines were non-functional and gh was the only working channel; a retry-after-40s was attempted but the sandbox blocks standalone Start-Sleep, so I stopped rather than force it). Recommendation for future scouts: use Brave Search (search.brave.com/search?q=...) as the primary WebFetch fallback engine instead of Bing or DuckDuckGo when WebSearch is exhausted. On substance: true committed multi-year listing-ID-level panels compiled independently of Inside Airbnb are rare on GitHub; almost everything found either (a) re-uses Inside Airbnb data at one or a few vintages with a churn/survival label bolted on, or (b) is Tom Slee's pre-Inside-Airbnb scraper/dataset, which is genuinely the best find here for the pre-2015-2017 historical gap. I did not find a GitHub replication package for the published 'longitudinal cohort study on listing survival' academic paper (Taylor & Francis) — it may exist behind the paper's supplementary materials rather than on GitHub; a future scout with journal access could check the paper's data-availability statement directly rather than searching GitHub blind.
